brief: QQQ has crossed its 50-day moving average 13 times since August 4, 2026, and on the 31st trading day since then remains within that day's range. Historically, when QQQ opens above its 20- and 50-day averages after starting below them, as it did today, it returns a median +1.13% over the next 5 days (positive 73% of the time) but reverses to a median -1.95%/-1.5% by 30-40 days out (negative 70% of the time), so BTIG reads the setup as short-term bullish, medium-term bearish. The chop reflects breadth divergence: the NDX is roughly flat since mid-August, but the share of names above their 200-day average fell from 77% to 56%. Within AI/semis, AMD, Qorvo, and Skyworks are back near 52-week highs while Lam Research, Applied Materials, and Western Digital remain 30-40% below their June highs, and SOXX stays below its declining 50-day average. BTIG concludes stock selection now carries more alpha than in Q2, when any semi worked, and bullish investors should favor names near new highs over laggards. Citing 2000, BTIG notes prior leaders that failed to make new highs after that year's initial correction ultimately proved the true market signal.
